What's included

A basement is only as good as what's behind the drywall

Most basements in Peel, Halton and Hamilton were poured with no insulation on the walls and a slab sitting straight on gravel. Frame and drywall over that and you get a musty room with cold floors by February. We deal with the concrete first, then build the room.

Before we price anything, we check the foundation for moisture, look at the sump and the grading outside, and confirm your panel can take the new circuits. If there's a water problem, you hear about it at the site visit, not after the drywall is up.

  • Envelope

    • DMX or Delta-FL dimpled membrane on foundation walls
    • Stud walls held off the concrete
    • ROCKWOOL batts and vapour control where code calls for it
    • Insulated subfloor panels over the slab

  • Mechanical

    • New circuits, pot lights and a subpanel if needed
    • Heating and return air extended to every room
    • Rough-in for a bathroom, wet bar or laundry
    • Egress windows cut and installed

  • Finishes

    • Drywall, tape and paint
    • LVP, engineered or tile flooring
    • Doors, trim and baseboard
    • Bathroom tile over Schluter waterproofing

  • Second suites

    • Fire separation between units
    • Interconnected smoke and CO alarms
    • Separate entrance where the layout allows
    • Permit drawings and inspections

How we build it

How we finish a basement, in order

Six stages. Inspections happen between them, so nothing gets closed in before the city has seen it.

  1. Moisture check and measure

    We look for efflorescence and damp spots, check grading and downspouts outside, and measure every wall and ceiling height. Low spots under ductwork get flagged now.

  2. Drawings and permit

    Layout drawings go to you first, then to the city if a permit is needed. Permit review times vary by city and season, and we build that into the start date.

  3. Envelope

    Membrane on the walls, framing held off the concrete, subfloor over the slab. You never see this part, and it matters most.

  4. Rough-in and inspection

    Electrical, plumbing and ductwork go in, and the inspector sees all of it before any wall is closed.

  5. Insulation, drywall and finishes

    ROCKWOOL and vapour control, drywall, then flooring, trim and paint.

  6. Final inspection and walkthrough

    The permit gets closed, you get the paperwork, and we walk the space with you before the final invoice.

Cost

What a basement renovation costs

We don't quote by the square foot over the phone, because two basements the same size can be far apart in price. These are the things that move the number.

Every quote is a fixed price for your house, with HST shown as its own line.

Get your fixed price

  • WaterAn active leak or damp wall has to be fixed, from outside or with interior drainage, before finishing.
  • Ceiling heightDuctwork and beams that need boxing in, or a floor that needs lowering, add labour.
  • A bathroomBreaking the slab for drains is the biggest single line in most basement quotes.
  • A second suiteFire separation, egress, a separate entrance and permit drawings add cost. They also add rent.
  • Finish levelLVP or engineered, hollow or solid-core doors, a wet bar or not.

Plan on [X weeks] on site for a typical finish once the permit is in hand, and [X weeks] for a legal second suite. Inspections are booked as we go, so the schedule on your quote already includes them.

In most cases, yes. Ontario allows a second unit in most detached houses, semis and townhouses, subject to the Ontario Building Code and your city's zoning rules. It needs fire separation, egress windows, interconnected alarms and a permit. We confirm your address qualifies before you spend anything on drawings.

LVP, in most cases. It is waterproof and floats over a subfloor or membrane on the slab. Engineered hardwood can work over a dry slab with a proper subfloor, but solid hardwood should not go below grade.
